By default, this API server endpoint is public to the internet, and access to the API server is secured using a combination of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) along with native Kubernetes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Enabling private access to the Kubernetes API server ensures that all communication between your nodes and the API server stays within your VPC. You can limit the IP addresses that have access to your API server from the internet, or you can completely disallow internet access to the API server\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/eks-rules.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Configuring control plane egress routing\",\"context\":\"## IAM condition key\\n\\nAmazon EKS supports the `eks:controlPlaneEgressMode` condition key. You can use this key in IAM policies or service control policies (SCPs) to control which egress mode callers can specify when they create or update clusters.\\n\\nThe condition key applies to the following actions:\\n\\n* `eks:CreateCluster`\\n* `eks:UpdateClusterConfig`\\n\\nFor example, the following SCP denies cluster creation and configuration updates unless the caller specifies `CUSTOMER_ROUTED`:\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\": \\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"RequireCustomerRoutedControlPlane\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Deny\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"eks:CreateCluster\\\",\\n \\\"eks:UpdateClusterConfig\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": \\\"*\\\",\\n \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n \\\"StringNotEquals\\\": {\\n \\\"eks:controlPlaneEgressMode\\\": \\\"CUSTOMER_ROUTED\\\"\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nUse this policy to enforce that all new and updated clusters in your organization use the `CUSTOMER_ROUTED` egress mode\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-egress.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Verify CIS EKS Benchmark 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 wording"}

{"id": "66cf238b-bfbf-43e3-be46-cc6c71552002", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Result: 5.4.1 passes and 5.4.2 fails.** I checked only the three endpoint values you gave me, against my reading of the two controls. | Control | Requirement | Your values | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.4.1 Restrict access to the control plane endpoint | Private access enabled, and public access limited to specific CIDRs, not `0.0.0.0/0` | `endpointPrivateAccess=true`, `publicAccessCidrs=["203.0.113.0/24"]` | **Pass** |
| 5.4.2 Private endpoint enabled and public access disabled | Private access on and public access off | `endpointPublicAccess=true` | **Fail** |

- **5.4.1:** Nodes reach the API server privately, and internet access is limited to one /24. The result depends on that range being your real allow-list. `203.0.113.0/24` is the reserved TEST-NET-3 documentation block. If it is a placeholder, or it isn't your actual office or VPN egress range, treat 5.4.1 as unverified.
- **5.4.2:** This control requires public access to be off, and a CIDR allow-list doesn't satisfy it. The cluster would pass only with `endpointPublicAccess=false`. Changing that means you must reach the API server from inside the VPC, for example over VPN, Direct Connect or a bastion. Otherwise the cluster becomes unmanageable from outside.

**Framework rows:** I can't tell you which rows these two controls feed. The closest AWS-side control is Control Tower proactive control CT.EKS.PR.1, which requires public access to the API endpoint to be disabled. That matches 5.4.2's intent, so you would likely fail it as well. It is a related control, not a documented row that the CIS controls feed.
